source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Single, 70: IRA distributions 10,000 and a Roth conversion 20,000 (both federally taxable; the conversion is in federal AGI). The booklet does not say whether a conversion counts for line 16; the projection leaves conversions out, so line 16 is the IRA 10,000 only. If the conversion counted, line 16 would be 24,000. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (you) 10,000.00 + roth conversion (you) 20,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 = 12,250.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 30,000.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 30,000.00. Schedule SB: line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 70): IRA 10,000.00 = 10,000.00; smaller of 10,000.00 and the 24,000.00 cap = 10,000.00; line 50 total 10,000.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 30,000.00 is not less than 15,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 10,000.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 30,000.00 - 10,000.00 = 20,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 20,000 to less than 20,500, column Single: 13,476.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 20,000 / 20,500 / 13,476 / 25,110 / 10,573 / 17,362). Line 9 = 20,000.00 - 13,476.00 = 6,524.00. Line 10a 1 x 700 = 700.00; line 10b 1 x 250 = 250.00; line 10c 950.00. Line 11 taxable income = 6,524.00 - 950.00 = 5,574.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule A (single) as numbers: 3.5% x 5,574.00 = 195.09; total 195.09, rounded once to 195.09. The Tax Table row 5,500 to 5,600 (PDF page 38) gives 194; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 195.09.
accepted_approximations: Roth conversions are left out of both retirement subtractions (covers_unclear: the booklets do not say whether a conversion counts, though the 5,000 worksheet takes federal Form 1040 line 4b).
The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
